adScenario.autobahn_ueberholen: Three-lane highway: a slower vehicle on the right lane is overtaken on the left, then the ego returns to the right lane (keep-right rule).
adScenario.einfaedeln_lkw: Highway entry after Werling 5.3.2: merging from the acceleration lane into the gap between two trucks.
adScenario.einscherer: A slower vehicle cuts in from the left 22 m ahead of the ego.
adScenario.innerorts_werling: Urban road after Werling 5.3.1 at 30 km/h: parked cars, two pedestrians step onto the road from between parked cars and are visible late, an oncoming vehicle turns left wrongly at the junction, two cyclists at the roadside.
adScenario.kreisverkehr: Single-lane roundabout: entry from the west, yielding to the traffic in the ring, exit to the east.
adScenario.kreuzung_ampel_geradeaus: The ego approaches at red, stops at the stop line and drives straight on at green; cross traffic drives during the ego's red phase.
adScenario.kreuzung_vorfahrt_links: The ego comes from the minor road, yields to the cross traffic and turns left.
adScenario.laengsparken_rueckwaerts: Reverse parallel parking into an 8.5 m gap: forward beside the gap, stop, change of direction at standstill, reverse to the middle of the gap.

adScenario.notausweichen_hindernis: A broken-down vehicle becomes visible only 60 m ahead; evasion onto the free left lane.
adScenario.verkehrsdichte_20: Three-lane ring road with 20 vehicles per km and lane, IDM car following and MOBIL lane changes, 10 % trucks.
adScenario.werling_autobahnversuch: Highway experiment after Werling 5.3.2: merging between trucks, a delayed lane change because of a fast approaching car, a truck pulling out and a side-wind gust (lateral_impulse) at t = 38.5 s.

adScenarioLabel.ausscherer_stauende: Cut-out at the end of a queue

tracking_controller.composite: Combination of a lateral and a longitudinal controller

assumptions: Constant step dt (component period or executor step)
steering_powertrain.expert: The integration of $\dot\delta$ is limited (anti-windup), so that the integrator does not run away at the steering stop.
limitations: The characteristic error acts on the curvature tan(delta)/l (as in vdsim.actuators)
steering_powertrain.purpose: Connects the outputs of the trajectory controller with the plant.
steering_powertrain.summary: Integrates the steering rate or takes the steering angle, and models the steering actuator (latency, characteristic, rate limit) and delayed drive and brake torques.

assumptions: Map knowledge (lanes, markings, stop lines) is known exactly
Objects carry lane_id/s/d from the scenario engine or the perception
limitations: no replanning of the route after a missed exit
Left turn on green: simple gap check against oncoming traffic
rule_based.purpose: Behavior layer after Werling 3.6: choose the targets so that the reactive trajectory planning rarely has to avoid a collision.
rule_based.summary: State machine for lane keeping, lane changes, merging, overtaking, intersections, roundabouts and parking; it provides the reference curve, the longitudinal modes and the corridor for the trajectory planner.
rule_based.theory: Lane change in the manner of MOBIL: $\tilde a_c - a_c + p(\tilde a_n - a_n) \pm a_{bias} > \Delta a_{th}$ with IDM accelerations and a safety check on the prediction. Merging: gap centre $s_{ref} = \tfrac12 (s_a + s_b)$ (3.15), gap selection by the required acceleration. Right of way: gap acceptance with the predicted occupancy of the conflict zones.

ground_truth.purpose: Reference for developing prediction, behavior and planning without perception errors.
ground_truth.summary: Passes on the objects of the scenario engine and the true ego state unchanged.

assumptions: Objects as rectangles, occlusion only in the plane (no height information)
Noise is white and normally distributed, objects are independent
limitations: no tracking, no false alarms (ghost objects)
no fusion of several sensors
object_sensor.purpose: More realistic inputs for prediction and behavior: limited range, occlusion, measurement noise, missed detections and latency; reproducible through the scenario seed.
object_sensor.summary: Creates a disturbed object list and an estimate of the ego state from the ground truth.
object_sensor.theory: Polar measurement model: $r_m = r + n_r$, $\varphi_m = \varphi + n_\varphi$ with $n \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)$, plus additive noise on position, speed, orientation and acceleration. An object is visible if one corner lies within range, it intersects the field of view and it is not mostly hidden by closer objects.

assumptions: Acceleration constant over the horizon
no lateral motion relative to the lane
at a branch the object follows the default continuation of the lane
limitations: Lane changes and turns of other road users are not predicted
constant_acceleration.purpose: Prediction of leading and gap vehicles for the following and merging modes after Werling 3.5.2.
constant_acceleration.summary: Predicts objects with constant acceleration along their lane in Frenet coordinates.
constant_acceleration.theory: $s_v(t) = s_v(0) + \dot s_v(0) t + \tfrac12 \ddot s_v(0) t^2$, $d(t) = d(0)$; for $\dot s_v(t) \le 0$ the standstill is held. Objects without a lane are predicted in Cartesian coordinates along their orientation.

constant_velocity.purpose: Simple reference prediction that needs no map, for example for pedestrians.
constant_velocity.summary: Straight-line prediction with constant speed (optionally constant yaw rate).
constant_velocity.theory: $x(t) = x_0 + v \cos\psi\, t$, $y(t) = y_0 + v \sin\psi\, t$; with CTRV $\psi(t) = \psi_0 + \dot\psi t$.

assumptions: Objects follow the default continuation of the lane
limitations: Turning intentions at intersections are not estimated
lane_following.purpose: Detects lane changes (cut-ins) early from the lateral speed relative to the lane.
lane_following.summary: Constant speed along the lane sequence; the lateral offset converges to the center of the target lane.
lane_following.theory: Longitudinal: $s(t) = s_0 + \dot s_0 t$ (optionally with $\ddot s_0$). Lateral: critically damped $d(t) = d_z + (e_0 + (\dot d_0 + e_0/\tau) t) e^{-t/\tau}$ with $e_0 = d_0 - d_z$. The target offset $d_z$ is the centre of the neighbouring lane if $|\dot d_0|$ exceeds the intention threshold and the object moves towards it, otherwise the centre of its own lane.

assumptions: Leading vehicle inside the driving corridor of the trajectory
acc.expert: String stability for $\tau>0$ and suitable gains (Rajamani ch. 5).
limitations: Freedom from collision is not guaranteed
acc.purpose: Comparison of trajectory-based longitudinal control with a classical ACC without a planner.
acc.summary: Distance-based longitudinal control with a constant time gap.

assumptions: Lateral and longitudinal dynamics decoupled
composite.expert: Stability follows from the partial controllers only for weak coupling.
limitations: Coupling (friction circle) not considered
composite.purpose: Classical decoupled lateral and longitudinal control as a comparison with the coupled Werling control.
composite.summary: Combines any lateral and any longitudinal controller into one tracking controller.

assumptions: Forward driving
ff_fb.expert: Error dynamics $\ddot e_t+k_v\dot e_t+k_se_t=0$, stable for $k_v,k_s>0$.
limitations: Actuator limits only clamped
ff_fb.purpose: Time-based longitudinal tracking (trajectory instead of path).
ff_fb.summary: Acceleration feedforward from the trajectory with feedback of the speed and longitudinal errors.

assumptions: Linear tires, small angles, forward driving
lqr.expert: For every fixed $v$ the closed discrete loop $A_d-B_dK$ is asymptotically stable (stabilizable pair, $Q\geq0$ observable); slow gain scheduling preserves stability.
limitations: Linearization, model singular for v -> 0 (v_min)
lqr.summary: State feedback on the lateral error model of the single-track model with a discrete Riccati solution, gain scheduling over speed and a steady-state feedforward.
lqr.theory: $x=[e_1,\dot e_1,e_2,\dot e_2]$, $u=-Kx+\delta_{ff}$, $K$ from the DARE of the model discretized with ZOH, $\delta_{ff}=l\kappa+K_V v^2\kappa-k_3e_{2,ss}$.

assumptions: Kinematics with understeer gradient (quasi-stationary yaw dynamics)
Forward driving
mpc.expert: Recursive feasibility is not guaranteed by the box constraints alone; stable in practice with a sufficiently long horizon (Rawlings/Mayne).
limitations: No stability proof without terminal cost or terminal constraint
Higher computing effort
mpc.purpose: Comparison controller that takes actuator limits into account explicitly (Werling Tab. 4.1).
mpc.summary: Linear time-varying model predictive lateral control along the trajectory horizon with limits on steering angle and steering rate.
mpc.theory: States $[e_y,e_\psi,\delta]$, input $\dot\delta$; $\dot e_y=v_ke_\psi$, $\dot e_\psi=v_k(\delta/(l+EG\,v_k^2)-\kappa_k)$ with $v_k,\kappa_k$ of the reference trajectory at the times of the horizon; condensed QP, solved with ADMM.

assumptions: Forward driving
pi.expert: Closed loop similar to a second-order lag, stable for $K_P,K_I>0$.
limitations: No feedforward
pi.summary: PI controller on the speed error.

assumptions: Forward driving
pid.expert: Stable for positive gains on the integrator $\dot v=a$.
limitations: No feedforward, following error in e_t
pid.summary: PID controller on the speed error of the planned trajectory.

assumptions: Kinematic vehicle, forward driving
pure_pursuit.expert: For small errors Pure Pursuit corresponds to a proportional controller on the lateral error with gain $2/L_d^2$; stability follows from the positive look-ahead (Snider 2009).
limitations: Cuts corners, stationary lateral error with a long look-ahead
No reversing
pure_pursuit.summary: Geometric lateral controller: a circular arc from the rear axle to a target point on the path.

assumptions: Forward driving
speed_pi.expert: The back-calculation limits the integrator in saturation (Åström/Hägglund).
limitations: No position error
speed_pi.purpose: Robust speed controller under actuator saturation.
speed_pi.summary: PI speed controller with back-calculation anti-windup and feedforward.

assumptions: Forward driving
stanley.expert: For the kinematic model the error at the front axle converges exponentially, $\dot e=-v\sin(\arctan(ke/v))$ (Hoffmann et al. 2007).
limitations: No reversing, kinematic derivation
stanley.purpose: Comparison controller with good tracking at medium speeds.
stanley.summary: Lateral controller on the lateral error of the front axle and the heading error (Stanley, DARPA Grand Challenge).

assumptions: The planner switches reference_point with hysteresis around v_s (contracts.md section 7)
The planner answers reinit_request with a trajectory with reinitialized=True
werling_bilevel.expert: Each partial controller is asymptotically stable on its own (theorems 4, 6, 8). Because both models are valid at the moment of switching and the feedforward parts dominate, the jumps stay small; the reinitialization sets the low-level errors to zero (Werling 2.3).
limitations: Hard switching: small jumps of the control input are possible, gains are matched
Thresholds c_t, c_n found by experiment (defaults for the mid-size sedan)
werling_bilevel.purpose: Combines the low-level stabilization (permanent disturbances, model errors) with the high-level stabilization by re-initialization after impulse disturbances (Werling 2.3, 4.4, 4.5).
werling_bilevel.summary: Default tracking controller: bumpless switching between the three Werling controllers by reference point and driving direction, plus the trigger of re-initializations and the motion prediction for the planner.
werling_bilevel.theory: Switching according to fig. 4.13; elliptic measure $(\dot e_t/c_t)^2+(\dot e_n/c_n)^2\geq1$ (4.5.1) at the centre of gravity or the geometric centre; Taylor prediction of the reference point over the planning latency (4.5.2).

assumptions: Flat road, no dynamic wheel loads (single-track model)
Tire parameters A, B, C per axle known (certainty equivalence)
Drive and brake forces controlled quickly, force ratio gamma known
v > 0 (forward driving, singular at v = 0)
werling_dynamic.expert: After the linearization $\ddot{\tilde e}_t=\tilde w_2$, $\ddot{\tilde e}_n=\tilde w_1$ holds; with (4.68)/(4.69) and $k>0$ the errors converge exponentially. The zero dynamics (4.67) are stable for $\lambda>\max(-l_h,-J/[l_vm])$ (theorem 9), their damping $\zeta$ is kept constant through (4.70).
limitations: Only local (tire saturation, condition (4.49))
Actuator limits are not part of the control law
Zero dynamics analysed linearly only for straight driving (theorem 9)
werling_dynamic.purpose: Stabilizes a reference point ahead of the center of gravity on the planned trajectory; the speed-dependent look-ahead keeps the damping of the zero dynamics constant (Werling 4.3).
werling_dynamic.summary: Exactly input-output linearizing tracking controller on the dynamic single-track model with an isotropic Pacejka tire, for fast driving.
werling_dynamic.theory: Output (4.46), invariant errors (4.48), relative degree [2,2], linearizing feedback as the solution of (4.60) (2D Newton), linear stabilization (4.68)/(4.69), zero dynamics (4.67), lambda(zeta, v_d) (4.70), online simulation of the zero dynamics (4.71)-(4.74), steering rate control (4.75).

assumptions: Kinematic single-track model, |beta~| < pi/2 (met by the steering angle limit)
Forward driving only, |kappa_d| < 1/lambda (theorem 7)
werling_kinematic_center.expert: With $\tilde V=\frac{1}{2}[\tilde k_1\tilde e_t^2+\tilde k_1\tilde e_n^2+\tilde e_\theta^2+\tilde e_v^2]$ and $\tilde w_2=\dot{\tilde v}_d-\tilde k_3\tilde e_v-\tilde k_1[\tilde e_t\cos\tilde e_\theta+\tilde e_n\sin\tilde e_\theta]$ it follows that $\dot{\tilde V}=-\tilde k_4\tilde e_\theta^2-\tilde k_3\tilde e_v^2\leq0$ (theorem 6). Zero dynamics (4.36) stable for $v_d>0$, $|\kappa_d|<1/\lambda$ (theorem 7).
limitations: Zero dynamics unstable in reverse (jackknife effect)
Orientation stable only through the zero dynamics (|psi - psi_d| <= pi/2 at the start)
werling_kinematic_center.purpose: Stabilizes the point about half a wheelbase ahead of the rear axle directly, so the vehicle steers more calmly (Werling 4.2.4).
werling_kinematic_center.summary: Lyapunov-based tracking controller of the geometric vehicle center without orientation stabilization, for slow forward driving.
werling_kinematic_center.theory: Flatness-based transformation of the reference (4.20)-(4.24), invariant errors of the vehicle centre (4.25), error dynamics of model 3 (4.26)/(4.27), control law (4.30)/(4.31) with the inverses (4.28)/(4.29) and back-substitution (4.7).

assumptions: No tire slip angles (slow driving, kinematic single-track model)
All states measured, steering angle |delta| < pi/2
Drive and brake forces are set quickly by subordinate control loops
werling_kinematic_orientation.expert: With $V_c=\frac{1}{2}[k_1e_t^2+k_1e_n^2+e_\psi^2+e_v^2+e_\delta^2]$, $\dot V_c=-\dot s_dk_2e_\psi^2-k_3e_v^2-k_4e_\delta^2\leq0$ holds; LaSalle gives asymptotic stability of $[e_t,e_n,e_\psi,e_v,e_\delta]=0$ for $\dot s_d\ne0$ (theorem 4). Forward and reverse through $\varsigma$, no jump of the steering angle at standstill because there is no division by $v$.
limitations: The front swings out during large corrections (reference point at the rear axle)
No actuator limit in the control law (reserve through the planning)
Unsuitable for fast driving (slip neglected)
werling_kinematic_orientation.purpose: Stabilizes position, orientation, speed and steering angle of the extended kinematic single-track model along the trajectory, also at standstill and in reverse (Werling 4.2.3).
werling_kinematic_orientation.summary: Lyapunov-based tracking controller of the rear-axle center with orientation stabilization, for slow forward and reverse driving.
werling_kinematic_orientation.theory: Invariant errors in the Frenet frame of the reference trajectory (4.9), fictitious control law for $\kappa_\delta$ (4.11), virtual input $w_2=\dot v$ (4.12), backstepping to $u_1=\dot\delta$ (4.16)-(4.18), back-substitution (4.15), (4.7).

limitations: no temporal consistency: the result depends on the replanning frequency
Control errors are set to zero in every cycle (no low-level robustness)
frenet_naive.purpose: Shows the benefit of temporal consistency (Werling Fig. 3.2) in planner comparisons.
frenet_naive.summary: Comparison planner: Frenet sampling with a relative end-time grid and replanning from the measured state.

assumptions: Fast driving with d(t), velocity mode
limitations: Following, merging, stopping, slow driving and reversing are planned by the Werling planner
The cost distance to the teacher is measured, not bounded
learned.purpose: Learned planning with the safety of the Werling planner: if no local candidate is valid, or the best one lies on the border of the local set, the cycle searches completely.
learned.summary: A network proposes the trajectory (end offset, end speed, end times); the Werling planner builds only the candidates next to the proposal and checks them with its restrictions and collision check.
learned.theory: Imitation learning of the selection of the Werling planner; features: start state, task, curvature ahead, nearest objects, previous choice (Bellman principle).

limitations: Longitudinal candidates are sorted lexicographically before lateral candidates
sequential.purpose: Shows the advantage of the combined lateral and longitudinal optimization (evasion with matched braking).
sequential.summary: Comparison planner: the longitudinal motion without knowledge of the lateral motion, then the lateral motion (Werling 3.1).

assumptions: Side slip angle at the reference point = 0 for the collision check
Leading vehicles with constant acceleration (clamped at standstill)
Reference curve with continuous change of curvature (remark 4)
limitations: temporal consistency only with inactive constraints and purely consistent cost terms
Class of functions limited to a double change of course (no maze manoeuvres)
Change of direction (ς) only at standstill through the behavior layer
werling.purpose: Reactive, time-critical collision avoidance with combined longitudinal and lateral optimization, temporally consistent by Bellman's principle while no restriction is active (Werling 2011, ch. 3).
werling.summary: Trajectory planning after Werling: optimal polynomials in Frenet coordinates, discretized target manifolds on an absolute time grid, temporal consistency and bi-level stabilization.
werling.theory: Lateral and longitudinal motion are the output of an integrator chain; the jerk-optimal solutions are quintic polynomials (fixed end state) or quartic polynomials (free end position). End times and end offsets are discretized on the target manifold; the best combination that satisfies the constraints is searched lazily in ascending order of cost.

assumptions: Front-axle steering, low speed in parking mode
limitations: In the stack only reverse parallel parking
werling_parking.purpose: Parking maneuvers with changes of direction, which the Frenet planner cannot represent on the reference line.
werling_parking.summary: Werling planner for normal driving; for a parking task a Hybrid A* / Reeds-Shepp planner plans the parking path and hands it to the controller one move at a time.
werling_parking.theory: Reeds-Shepp curves, Hybrid A*, multi-move exit; time parametrization with a steering rate limit.

assumptions: Powertrain dynamics neglected (torques act without delay, Werling 5.1.2.2)
Brake force distribution fixed at gamma (default 0.75)
split_range.expert: In steady state (constant disturbance F_s) and with the integrator active, $a\to a_{exp}$ holds because the integrator takes over the disturbance completely; in saturation its state stays bounded, so that there is no overshoot after leaving saturation.
limitations: No engine map F_M^-1 and no transmission drag torque (torque interface)
split_range.purpose: The design models of the tracking controllers neglect rolling and air resistance; this layer compensates them and removes remaining errors (head wind, slope) with an integrator.
split_range.summary: Converts the desired longitudinal force or acceleration into wheel torques through drive or brake.
split_range.theory: $u=F_{ld}+F_W(v)+k_I\int m(a_{exp}-a)\,dt$; $u\varsigma\geq0$: drive (reverse gear for $\varsigma=-1$), otherwise brake. Anti-windup: the integration is halted when the actuator is saturated and the error drives further into saturation (Werling fig. 5.3).

assumptions: Control inputs constant over one executor step (zero-order hold)
vehicle_model.expert: Explicit integration (Euler/Heun/RK4) with substeps; the substep size is limited by the recommendation or stable_dt of the model (for example DESM: $h<2/\max(\lambda_i)$ with $\lambda\approx(c_v+c_h)/(mv)$), so that RK4 stays numerically stable.
limitations: Reversing only with werling_kesm, bicycle_kinematic (werling_desm only slowly)
Disturbance forces only for models with the states vy and r
vehicle_model.purpose: Any vehicle model (Werling design models, single-track, double-track, multibody) as the plant for controller development and robustness studies.
vehicle_model.summary: Wraps a registered vdsim vehicle model as the plant of the control chain.

assumptions: Ego outline as a rectangle; its centre lies midway between the axles (equal overhangs)
Actors react to the ego vehicle through IDM as soon as it occupies their lane
limitations: no vehicle dynamics of the actors (kinematic motion along the lane)
disturbances such as the crosswind gust are only reported as an event, not applied by the engine
scenario_engine.purpose: Reproducible test scenarios for the whole chain: actors with IDM/MOBIL, scripted triggers, traffic lights, collision and off-road detection, and disturbance events.
scenario_engine.summary: Simulates the road users of a scenario and provides the ground truth.
scenario_engine.theory: Synchronous update of all actors (accelerations from the state at time t, then integration with substeps $h \le h_{max}$). Collisions between oriented rectangles with the separating axis theorem (SAT).
